items.title: Quick Research (Delegate research and get a cited report) | AWS Quick: Zero to Hero 09
items.summary: Level 200. A handout on delegating research to AWS Quick Research and getting back a report with sources, for people who have started using AWS Quick. It covers what Research is and what it is for; the four steps (write the research objective, choose the research materials such as web search, uploaded files, and Quick assets, review and revise the plan, and read the report); using the report (following the numbered citations back to the files and web articles, adding comments and making a new version, summary styles, sharing and downloading as PDF or Word); running research on a schedule with the Research step in Quick Flows; and third-party data from Premium and Public providers. The running example researches ways to keep a monthly internal learning session going. The screens were taken on the web in English from one research run on fictional material. The appendix lists the statuses and admin settings, a glossary, and sources. Based on public documentation as of November 2026. Deck 09 (Let it run) of the series AWS Quick: Zero to Hero.

items.title: From chat to deliverables (Response modes, sources, docs, decks, and spreadsheets) | AWS Quick: Zero to Hero 04
items.summary: Level 200. A handout for people who use AWS Quick, an AI assistant for work, and want better answers and files from chat. It covers how to write a request with three parts (what you want, what Quick should look at, and the format), how to point Quick to materials with the data scope and attachments, the response modes Fast, Balanced, and Smart and thinking effort in the desktop app, and how to check answers with citations, Sources, and the explanation for number answers. It then shows how to create a Word invitation, a PowerPoint deck, and an Excel table in chat, how company brand templates work (Enterprise edition), what visual creation can do and where, and how to revise a file with follow-up requests. The running example is organizing an internal learning session, with screenshots from the English web and desktop apps. The appendix has request examples, a glossary, and sources. Based on public documentation as of November 2026. Deck 04 (Go deeper) of the series AWS Quick: Zero to Hero.

items.title: Always-on agents (Routines, the activity feed, Mission Control, and approvals) | AWS Quick: Zero to Hero 11
items.summary: Level 200. A handout for people who use the AWS Quick desktop app (AWS Quick on desktop) and want agents to keep working while they are away. Runs on its own: an agent with a routine runs in the cloud on a schedule and delivers results to the feed, even with your laptop closed (runs that use local tools need the computer on); choosing, action by action, what goes ahead without asking; and setting up a routine, with the example Outstanding RSVPs (every Monday at 8:30 AM). Get the results: the activity feed (notices, the briefing, and no agent hours for viewing), clearing the feed, Mission Control (all runs, Needs input, routines, and numbers), and agents waiting for input. Approvals and usage: tool permissions apply to routine runs too; Smart Approvals lets low-impact actions through and sends high-impact ones to you, grants no new access, is logged in AWS CloudTrail, and works on desktop and mobile only; and a routine uses agent hours every time it runs. Screens of the desktop app show the routine fields, a routine card, a feed notice, and the Mission Control popover. The appendix has routine limits, a glossary, and sources. Based on public documentation as of November 2026. Deck 11 (Let it run) of the series AWS Quick: Zero to Hero.

items.title: Quick Sight and apps (Ask questions about your data and build apps by describing them) | AWS Quick: Zero to Hero 08
items.summary: Level 200. A handout on AWS Quick Sight and apps in AWS Quick, for people who ask questions about their data and people who build small business apps for their team. It covers how plans differ; Quick Sight (connecting data and datasets with SPICE or Direct Query, asking a dashboard in chat and Dashboard Q&A, turning an answer into a Word document, executive summaries, generating an analysis from a description, and row-level and column-level security); and apps in Quick (describe, generate, preview, iterate, and publish; what an app can use, such as data storage, AI, Quick Sight visuals, connectors, and spaces; building a registration app for a learning session; using a dataset with approval; publishing and sharing with Limited, Account, or Public access; how apps stay safe; and what apps can't do, including Regions). The screens were taken on the web in English. The appendix lists app limits, a glossary, and sources. Based on public documentation as of November 2026. Deck 08 (Go deeper) of the series AWS Quick: Zero to Hero.

items.title: Spaces and knowledge (Get answers from your company's own documents) | AWS Quick: Zero to Hero 05
items.summary: Level 200. A handout on how to use spaces and knowledge bases so that AWS Quick answers from your team and company documents. A space brings files, knowledge bases, and more together in one place for a team or project. With a monthly internal learning session as the example, it shows on English screens of Quick on the web how to create a space, wait for Ready, ask and check the sources, and share it with roles (owner or viewer). Everyone a space is shared with can see the files uploaded to it, while dashboards and knowledge bases in Quick follow the permissions of the viewer. A knowledge base takes in content from sources such as SharePoint, Amazon S3, and Google Drive as an index and syncs it on a schedule. Diagrams and tables, not screens, explain how this works, document-level access control, the two ways to connect SharePoint (a knowledge base or a connector), and how index capacity is counted. Sharing a space needs a plan other than Free, and on company plans Enterprise users create knowledge bases. It also covers indexing local folders in the desktop app and bringing in an Amazon Q Business index or an Amazon Bedrock managed knowledge base. The appendix has the sources to connect and their limits, a glossary, and sources. Based on public documentation and screens as of November 2026. Deck 05 (Go deeper) of the series AWS Quick: Zero to Hero.

items.title: Strands harness (A ready-made agent and the Strands Harness SDK) | Learn Strands Agents with Kiro 10
items.summary: This Level 200 deck builds a ready-made agent with create_harness() of Strands harness (strands-harness), adds and narrows its tools and instructions, keeps conversations and knowledge with session and memory, and decides where it stops with interventions and a sandbox before you ship it, using the official docs and real output of strands-harness 0.3.4 on Amazon Bedrock in the Tokyo Region. It shows how Strands harness sits on the Strands Harness SDK, as deck 10 (Ship and extend) of the series Learn Strands Agents with Kiro, for developers who write Python and are new to Strands Agents.

items.title: Quick on desktop (Connect your files, email, and calendar) | AWS Quick: Zero to Hero 03
items.summary: Level 100. An introduction to AWS Quick on desktop, for business users who have started using AWS Quick. It explains what the desktop app adds to AWS Quick on the web (folders on your computer, your browser, and running code on your computer), and that email and calendar come through cloud connectors. It walks through installing, signing in, first-run setup, the home screen, the left rail, and response modes, with screens captured in English. Using a team's monthly learning session as the running scenario, it adds a folder in Customize, then Knowledge (adding a folder does not upload it, and you choose per folder whether to upload), asks for the action items in the meeting notes, and explains system tools and their three access levels (write actions ask each time by default). It also covers connecting your calendar and email, the Library and session tabs, My context (memories and the knowledge graph), and continuing on your phone. The appendix has desktop usage limits, a glossary, and sources. Based on public documentation and screens as of November 2026. Deck 03 (Get started) of the series AWS Quick: Zero to Hero.
